summary: The rotating profile that converts shaft rotation into timed valve motion through a follower, rocker or push rod.

variants.name: Separate cam lobes on a hollow chain-driven camshaft
variants.applies_to: Four-cylinder engine with rocker-operated exhaust valves (Wright 1903)
distinguishing_features: one separate lobe per exhaust valve
driven by a chain from a 6-tooth to a 12-tooth sprocket

dimensions.name: speed ratio, cam over crank
dimensions.basis: 12 cam teeth over 6 crank teeth gives two crank turns per cam turn.

dimensions.name: lobe count
dimensions.basis: One exhaust lobe per cylinder; inventory 36 lists ExhaustCam1 to ExhaustCam4.

construction.note: Lobe boss offset from the axis (illustrative dwell profile, not a cam curve)

function.role: Open the exhaust valves, once per two crank turns, through the rockers.
function.motion: Turns at half crank speed, driven by the chain; each lobe lifts its rocker once per revolution.

envelope.statement: Hollow shaft with locating washers and separate cam parts.
Lobe shape and valve phases are illustrative: the study offers no authenticated running animation.
envelope.basis: Inventory gaps, "Cam law and phases"; the lobes are built from cylinders.

intent.statement: Separate lobes let each one be located and phased on the shaft by washers.
intent.basis: Read from inventory 36; no source in the study states the reason.

manufacturing.process: hollow shaft with separate lobes and washers

instances.validation: Interference audit of the exported file is clean: 1,121 neighbouring pairs at rest, 133 poses of the baked clip, 0 overlaps (interference-audit.json); geometry is valid but historical accuracy is not verified (cad-validation.json).

gaps: Cam law and phases are unknown, so the lobe profile is a placeholder.
Chain pitch is a teaching estimate; the source confirms tooth counts, not the pitch.

variants.name: Annular double-lobe ring cam with an integral tooth ring
variants.applies_to: Five-cylinder radial with five punch-rod exhaust valves (Langley / Manly-Balzer)
distinguishing_features: one ring journalled on the outside of the port hub
tooth ring at its outboard end takes the drive
five rollers ride on one cam track

dimensions.name: cam rise
dimensions.basis: Valve lift 12.0 mm plus the documented gap; lift and lobe form are illustrative (part-spec.json cam_rise).

dimensions.name: lobe half width
dimensions.basis: Cam degrees; 28 cam degrees is 112 crank degrees (part-spec.json cam_lobe_half_width).

dimensions.name: cam-ring tooth count
dimensions.basis: Chosen with the rest of the train to give net -1/4 exactly (part-spec.json cam_train_module; langley_drive.py).

construction.note: Involute teeth on the ring, from a derived outline
Double-pointed cam track, from a derived outline
Lightening pockets in the tooth ring and the cam track

function.role: Lift all five exhaust valves from one component.
function.motion: Journalled on the port hub, turns at one quarter of crank speed in the reverse direction; two lobes pass each of five rollers in turn.

envelope.statement: A cam at minus one quarter of crank speed with two lobes is the only one that closes with the firing order 1-3-5-2-4; forward or half speed fail.
Hardened rollers on the cam; punch rods stand 1/64 in from the exhaust stems.

intent.statement: One double-lobed ring serves all five exhaust valves, so the engine needs a single cam and no camshaft.
intent.basis: The arrangement is documented (M1 p. 237; A1 p. 108); its purpose is not stated.

manufacturing.basis: The study records steel (part-spec.json) and cites no statement of material or process for the ring cam.

instances.validation: Interference audit of the exported file is clean: 1,492 neighbouring pairs at rest, 133 poses of the baked clip, 0 overlaps (interference-audit.json); mass check against the Memoir weight table in build-notes.md.

gaps: The form of the teeth is not documented and is drawn external (inventory L24).
